ads_ratio.reason: Direct-listed foreign private issuer: one NYSE-traded GFL share is one subordinate voting share, so no ADS conversion applies; per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis.
ads_ratio.source: Form 40-F cover (SEC filing, CIK 1780232): the securities registered and listed on the NYSE under symbol GFL are the company's subordinate voting shares themselves (company releases declare dividends 'for each outstanding subordinate voting share'; the same class trades on the TSX as GFL) — there is no depositary or ADS program, so the NYSE line is the share itself, not an ADS

moat_against: Larger, more profitable rivals (Waste Management, Republic Services, Waste Connections) with stronger margins and balance sheets
Growth is acquisition-led: 9.9pp of Q2 2026's 16.3% revenue growth came from M&A, with integration and overpayment risk on every deal (e.g. SECURE, closed Sep 1 2026)
Capex intensity: capex ran $833.6M against $961.2M of operating cash flow in FY2025 — the asset base consumes nearly all cash generation
Leverage and dual-class founder control: net debt $5.36B (engine figure, pre-SECURE) and founder/CEO holds outsized voting power via multiple voting shares
Recycled-commodity price and diesel exposure; volumes were a slight drag (-0.6pp) in Q2 2026
moat_for: Route density in collection markets — dense routes lower cost per stop and are hard for entrants to replicate profitably
Scarce permitted landfill and transfer-station assets; new landfill permits are extremely difficult to obtain
Long-term municipal and commercial contracts with demonstrated pricing power (core pricing +6.1% in Q2 2026)
Scale: fourth-largest diversified environmental services company in North America, 19 U.S. states plus Canada
moat_justification: North America's fourth-largest diversified environmental services company: route density in its collection markets, scarce permitted landfill assets, and long-term municipal/commercial contracts give real pricing power (core pricing +6.1% in Q2 2026) and moderate switching friction — but collection itself has low entry barriers, Waste Management / Republic Services / Waste Connections run larger and more profitable networks, growth has been bought via a debt-funded roll-up rather than earned organically (organic growth was 6.4% of Q2 2026's 16.3%), and the fleet/landfill base demands heavy, perpetual capex that consumes nearly all operating cash flow.
name: GFL Environmental Inc.
one_liner: Capex-heavy waste roll-up, moat 5/10 — normalized owner's earnings are only $0.04/share against a $43.55 price (weighted IRR -4.8%, weighted IV@15 $0.49), so it does not come close to clearing 15%; it would clear 15% only below ~$0.49 on this model.
sector: Utilities / Environmental services — solid waste management
